objectives: Hear /t/ followed immediately by /r/ at the beginning of a taught word.
Blend /t/ and /r/ smoothly without inserting a vowel between them.
Distinguish the initial tr blend from /t/ alone and other taught blends.
Say the complete word after blending the onset with the remaining sounds.
concepts: The initial tr blend contains /t/ followed by /r/.
Both consonant sounds remain audible in the blend.
No extra vowel belongs between /t/ and /r/.
Listening for the complete word confirms accurate blending.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the beginning of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
Joining speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Trip starts with /t/ followed by /r/; tap starts with /t/ alone.
Keep /t/ and /r/ together, then blend the rest of the word.

commonMistakes: Adding a vowel and saying tuh-rip instead of blending smoothly.
Leaving out /r/ and saying tip for trip.
Guessing before hearing the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Do not insert a vowel between the consonants.
Blend the onset with the rest of the word.
Check the complete word against the sounds.
revisionPoints: Trip and trap both begin with tr.
